summary: This document specifies how Multicast VPN Source-Active routes interoperate with customer MSDP Source-Active routes. This helps providers whose customers already use MSDP, since otherwise VPN-specific MSDP sessions are needed between Provider Edge routers that peer with the customer. It updates RFC 6514.

eli5.summary: Two groups use different ways to announce who is sending a broadcast. This document translates between them so the provider does not need to set up extra connections.

questions: what is the mvpn sa rp-address extended community
why are vpn specific msdp sessions not needed
subtitle: How a provider's multicast VPN and a customer's MSDP network can swap source announcements without extra sessions.

tldr.problem: A provider running multicast VPN (MVPN) learns about active sources through BGP Source-Active routes, while customers may use MSDP. Without glue, the provider edge routers need VPN-specific MSDP sessions with each other.
tldr.mechanism: A PE attaches an Extended Community carrying the RP address to each MVPN Source-Active route, and other PEs can turn received MVPN SA routes into MSDP SA messages for their customer peers.
tldr.outcome: The VPN-specific MSDP sessions between PEs are no longer needed, and redundant parallel MSDP and MVPN SA messages are avoided.

today: RFC 9081 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2021. It updates RFC 6514, and no later RFC obsoleting or updating it is recorded.

sections.title: The Gap Between MVPN and MSDP
sections.content:
In the "spt-only" mode of RFC 6514, provider edge (PE) routers find out about active customer sources through MVPN Source-Active (SA) routes and then join the shortest path tree for each (C-S,C-G) flow. These routes work much like MSDP Source-Active messages.

RFC 6514 only covers the receiving PE (PE2) joining trees. It does not say that PE2 should advertise MSDP SA messages to its own customer MSDP peers. PE2 would need its own MSDP session with the originating PE (PE1) to do that. Worse, PE2 could then originate redundant MVPN SA routes from those MSDP messages.

Such a PE-to-PE MSDP session is specific to a single VPN, while the BGP sessions carrying MVPN routes are not. The procedures also apply to Global Table Multicast.
sections.eli5: One router shouts news in one language and its neighbor only listens in another. Without a translator, they would need a private line just for each club.

sections.title: Why Bridge Them: RP Addresses and Benefits
sections.content:
Passing MVPN SA information on as MSDP SA messages removes the VPN-specific MSDP sessions between PEs. The RFC lists further benefits of a BGP-based solution:

  • MSDP SA refreshes are replaced with BGP hard state.
  • Route reflectors can be used instead of peer-to-peer sessions.
  • VPN extranet mechanisms from RFC 2764 can spread (C-S,C-G) information across VPNs with flexible policy control.

There is one catch. An MSDP SA carries the source, group and rendezvous point (RP) address, but an MVPN SA carries only source and group. MSDP needs the RP address for its peer Reverse Path Forwarding (RPF) check, so the RP address has to be added to the MVPN SA route.
sections.eli5: The old announcement slip had a line for the meeting spot, and the new one did not. This document adds that line back so the old system can still read it.

sections.title: Scope: spt-only Mode
sections.content:
The RFC covers the "spt-only" mode. The other approach, "rpt-spt" mode, is described in Section 13 of RFC 6514, where SA routes replace PIM-ASM assert and (s,g,rpt) prune mechanisms and are not used for source discovery.

Interoperation between MVPN and MSDP SA for the rpt-spt mode is explicitly outside the scope of this document.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to run the game. This document explains the translator for only one of them.

sections.title: The RP-address Extended Community
sections.content:
The MVPN PEs that act as customer RPs or have MSDP sessions in a VPN are treated as an MSDP mesh group, called the PE mesh group. It MUST NOT include other MSDP speakers and fits into the rest of the VPN's MSDP network by normal MSDP rules.

When a PE advertises an MVPN SA route in spt-only mode, it MUST attach an MVPN SA RP-address Extended Community. This is a Transitive IPv4-Address-Specific Extended Community with the Local Administrator field set to zero and the Global Administrator field set to an RP address:

  • If the source was learned through a PIM Register, the local RP address for the group is used.
  • If it was learned from an incoming MSDP SA message, the RP address in the selected message is used.
sections.eli5: Every announcement now gets a sticker saying which meeting spot it belongs to, so the old system knows where it came from.

sections.title: Generating MSDP SA Messages from MVPN SA Routes
sections.content:
A PE may be provisioned to generate MSDP SA messages from received MVPN SA routes, with or without local policy control. Such a route is treated as if an MSDP SA message had arrived from within the PE mesh group, and normal MSDP procedure follows, for example advertising to MSDP peers outside the mesh group. The (S,G) comes from the (C-S,C-G) in the NLRI and the RP address from the Extended Community.

If the route has no Extended Community, perhaps because it came from a legacy PE, the local RP address for the group is used. That RP could turn out to be the very MSDP peer receiving the message, which would discard it after an RPF failure. The peer SHOULD use local policy to accept the message.

A PE MAY act on only the best MVPN SA route chosen by BGP route selection. If that route lacks the Extended Community but another route for the same (C-S,C-G) has it, the next best route with the community SHOULD be chosen. If the selected route changes the RP address, a new MSDP SA is advertised, and the state for the old RP times out.
sections.eli5: When a router hears an announcement in the new language, it repeats it in the old language to its old-style friends. If the sticker is missing, it guesses the meeting spot from its own list.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC extends what RFC 6514 does in one direction (MSDP to MVPN SA) to the reverse direction (MVPN SA to MSDP SA). It concludes that this adds no security considerations beyond those of RFC 6514 and RFC 3618.

It also argues that the procedures remove the control message amplification that exists today, where VPN-specific MSDP sessions among PEs lead to redundant MSDP and MVPN SA messages being carried in parallel.
sections.eli5: The translator adds no new ways to cheat. It actually stops the same news from being passed along twice.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA registered value 0x20 in the "Transitive IPv4-Address-Specific Extended Community Sub-Types" registry, with the description "MVPN SA RP-address Extended Community".
sections.eli5: The new sticker got its own official number so nobody else uses it for something different.
